title: Potential difference calculation
description: Essential: The final answer for part (1) must be correctly derived and stated as U = 12mgL/q.

title: Charge polarity identification
description: Essential: The answer for part (2) must correctly identify the polarity of ball B's charge as negative.

title: Charge magnitude calculation
description: Essential: The answer for part (2) must correctly state the magnitude of the charge on ball B as (2/3)q.

title: Total time calculation
description: Essential: The final answer for part (3) must be correctly derived and stated as t = (6√3 - 5)√(L/g).

title: Work-energy theorem application
description: Important: The solution must correctly apply the work-energy theorem to relate the work done by the electric field to the system's kinetic energy.

title: Newton's second law for system
description: Important: The solution must correctly apply Newton's second law to find the acceleration of the two-ball system for different charge configurations in the electric field.

title: Kinematic stage analysis
description: Important: The solution must correctly break the motion into distinct stages (only A in field, both in field, only B in field) and apply kinematic equations for each.

title: Sign error in force
description: Pitfall: Incorrectly assigning the direction of the electric force on a negative charge, leading to a wrong sign for acceleration or polarity.

title: System mass oversight
description: Pitfall: Using the mass of a single ball (m) instead of the total system mass (2m) when applying Newton's second law to the connected system.

title: Unit consistency check
description: Optional: The final answers should have dimensionally consistent units (e.g., time proportional to √(L/g)).
